guide.habit: Give the agent the goal, context and limits up front
guide.why: a request with the goal, the context and the limits lets the agent get it right the first time.
guide.try_this: start with what done looks like, what it touches, and what it must not change.
guide.starter: Goal: <what done looks like>. Context: <files, background>. Limits: <what not to change>. Then: <the task>.

guide.habit: Say who the doc is for, what it must do, and its limits
guide.why: a draft aimed at a named reader and purpose needs far less rewriting.
guide.try_this: say who will read it, what they should do after, what to draw on, and the length or tone.
guide.starter: Write <doc> for <reader> so they can <decide or do what>. Use <sources>. Limits: <length, tone, what to leave out>.

guide.habit: Say why you're asking, what you know, and what to leave out
guide.why: the reason behind a question and what you already know let the agent answer the right question.
guide.try_this: say what you'll do with the answer, what you already know, and where not to look.
guide.starter: I'm asking because <decision or task>. I already know <what you know>. Look at <where>, not <where not>. Answer: <question>.

guide.habit: Say what was wrong before asking again
guide.why: rewording alone rarely changes the result; the agent needs something new to go on.
guide.try_this: when an answer misses, say what was wrong and add one example, file or constraint.
guide.starter: That missed because <what was wrong>. Here is <an example, file or constraint>. Try again with that.

guide.habit: Check the diff or run the tests before using the result
guide.why: a quick look at the diff or a test run catches most agent mistakes before they cost you.
guide.try_this: read the diff or run the tests before you use the change.
guide.starter: Show me the diff, then run <test command> and tell me what passed and failed.

guide.habit: Check drafted claims against a source
guide.why: drafted claims can sound right and be wrong; a source check keeps the doc true.
guide.try_this: ask the agent to list each claim with its source, then spot-check them.
guide.starter: List every factual claim in the draft with the source it came from. Mark any claim without a source.

guide.habit: Hand over the whole task with a done test
guide.why: an agent with the whole task and a done test can plan the steps itself.
guide.try_this: give the whole outcome and how you'll know it's done, then review the result.
guide.starter: <The whole change>. Done means <test or check that passes>. Make all the edits, then show me the diff.

guide.habit: Ask for the whole draft with what done means
guide.why: asking for the whole draft with what done means lets the agent keep it consistent.
guide.try_this: ask for the complete draft and say what a finished one must contain.
guide.starter: Write the whole <doc>. Done means it covers <sections> for <reader>. Then list what you were unsure of.

guide.habit: Let the agent write the doc in the file
guide.why: when the agent writes the file, you review one draft instead of moving text back and forth.
guide.try_this: point the agent at the file and let it write there, then review the changes.
guide.starter: Write <doc> in <file path>. Use <notes or sources>. When you're done, tell me what you changed and what you were unsure of.

guide.habit: Give all your notes at once, then review the draft
guide.why: all your notes in one go let the agent shape the whole draft, and you review it once.
guide.try_this: collect your changes into one message, then review the next draft as a whole.
guide.starter: Revise <doc> with all of these: <change>, <change>, <change>. Then show me the full draft and list what you changed.

guide.habit: Let the agent make the edits
guide.why: when the agent makes the edits, you review one result instead of steering each step.
guide.try_this: let the agent edit the files, and review the diff when it's done.
guide.starter: Make the change in <files> yourself. When you're done, show me the diff and what you checked.

guide.habit: Check the answer before acting on it
guide.why: an answer can sound sure and still be wrong; one check against a source catches most of it.
guide.try_this: ask where the answer comes from, and check one source or run before you act on it.
guide.starter: Answer <question>. Show the source, file or command each point comes from, and say how sure you are.

guide.habit: Ask the whole question and say what a good answer covers
guide.why: the whole question and what a good answer covers lets the agent dig in and report back once.
guide.try_this: say what you need to decide and what a good answer must cover, then let the agent find it.
guide.starter: I need to decide <decision>. Find out <question>. A good answer covers <points>, with sources.

guide.habit: Let the agent look it up itself
guide.why: an agent that reads the files, logs or docs itself often finds what a pasted excerpt leaves out.
guide.try_this: point the agent at where to look instead of pasting the material in.
guide.starter: Look in <files, logs or docs> to answer <question>. Tell me what you read and what you found.

guide.habit: Ask once with everything you need, then let it dig
guide.why: one full ask lets the agent plan its search instead of waiting for your next nudge.
guide.try_this: put the follow-ups you expect into the first ask, then read the whole answer.
guide.starter: Find out <question>. Also cover <follow-up> and <follow-up>. Report back once, with sources.

guide.habit: Say what should run, where, and what must not break
guide.why: an agent that knows what should run, where, and what must not break avoids most failed runs.
guide.try_this: say what should be running or released, in which place, and what must stay untouched.
guide.starter: Goal: <what should be running or released>. Where: <app, environment, account>. Must not: <what must not break or change>. Then: <the task>.

guide.habit: Check it really runs before you move on
guide.why: a command can succeed while the app, release or tool still does not work.
guide.try_this: ask for proof it worked: the status, the page loading, the version or the log line.
guide.starter: After <the step>, show me proof it worked: the status, the URL loading, the version number or the log line.

guide.habit: Hand over the whole run with a done check and a stop
guide.why: an agent with the whole run, a done check and a stop point can do the steps and still leave you the risky one.
guide.try_this: give the whole outcome, how you'll know it's done, and the step where it must stop and ask.
guide.starter: Do <the whole release or run>. Done means <the check that passes>. Stop and ask before <the risky step>.

guide.habit: Let the agent run the commands
guide.why: an agent that runs the commands sees the errors itself and can fix them before it hands back.
guide.try_this: let the agent run the commands and report what each printed.
guide.starter: Run the commands yourself to <goal>. Tell me each command and what it printed.

guide.habit: Give the whole run up front, not one command at a time
guide.why: with the whole run up front, the agent can do the steps and fix errors before it hands back.
guide.try_this: say the end state and the steps you expect, then let it run and report.
guide.starter: Get <app or release> to <end state>. Steps I expect: <step>, <step>. Stop and ask before <risky step>. Report each command and what it printed.

guide.habit: Give the agent a written brief or instructions file
guide.why: a written brief or instructions file carries the context every time, so the agent can plan alone.
guide.try_this: save the goal, rules and checks for this kind of task in a file and point the agent at it.
guide.starter: Read <brief or instructions file>. Plan the steps, do them, and check each one against the brief.

guide.habit: Ask the agent to run the tests itself
guide.why: an agent that runs the checks can fix what fails before it hands back.
guide.try_this: ask the agent to run the tests and keep fixing until they pass.
guide.starter: <The task>. Run the tests with <command>. Keep fixing until they all pass, then show me the diff and the test output.

guide.habit: Ask the agent to check the doc itself
guide.why: an agent that runs the link and style checks can fix what fails before it hands back.
guide.try_this: ask the agent to run the doc checks, such as links and spelling, and fix what fails.
guide.starter: <The doc task>. Then run <doc check, such as markdownlint or a link check> and fix what fails. Show me the output.

guide.habit: Ask the agent to run the health check itself
guide.why: an agent that runs the smoke test or health check can fix what fails before it hands back.
guide.try_this: name the check that proves it works, and ask the agent to run it after each step.
guide.starter: <The run or release>. After each step, run <smoke test or health check>. Fix what fails, then show me the output.

guide.habit: Split the work with an automated check between steps
guide.why: an automated check between steps catches a bad step before the next one builds on it.
guide.try_this: split the work into steps for sub-agents, with a test or check the agent runs between them.
guide.starter: Split <the task> into steps. Give each step to a sub-agent, and run <check> after each before going on.

guide.habit: Split a big question across sub-agents
guide.why: sub-agents can each look into one part, and you get one combined answer back.
guide.try_this: ask the agent to split the question and send a sub-agent to each part.
guide.starter: Split <question> into parts. Send a sub-agent to each, then combine what they found into one answer with sources.

guide.habit: Ask the agent to prove its answer with a run
guide.why: an answer the agent has proved with a command, query or test can be reused without checking again.
guide.try_this: ask the agent to prove each finding with a command, query or test it runs.
guide.starter: Answer <question>. For each finding, run <command, query or test> that proves it, and show the output.

guide.habit: Save it as a workflow others can run
guide.why: a saved, versioned workflow runs the same way every time, for you and for others.
guide.try_this: save the brief, the steps and the checks as a prompt file or script, and share it.
guide.starter: Turn what we just did into a reusable <prompt file or script> in <path>: its inputs, steps, checks, and when to stop and ask.
